excerpt: Scentbird is a US perfume subscription that sends a month's supply of a designer fragrance in an 8 ml vial. Pricing, history, funding and alternatives.
content:
Scentbird is a fragrance subscription service in the United States. Instead of buying a full bottle, subscribers pick a designer or niche perfume or cologne each month and receive about a month's supply in a small vial that fits a reusable travel spray case. TechCrunch described the format in 2015 as an 8 ml bottle of roughly 120 sprays. The catalogue has grown from about 500 fragrances in 2018, Beauty Independent reported, to about 900 designer and indie scents in Modern Retail's 2025 coverage; Scentbird's own site has advertised over 1,000. Brands shown on its pages include Gucci, Burberry, Dolce & Gabbana, Versace and Prada.

Cosmetics Business reported that Scentbird was founded in 2014 by Mariya Nurislamova, Sergei Gusev, Andrei Rebrov and Rachel ten Brink; Beauty Matter gives the launch year as 2013. Nurislamova is CEO. The company went through Y Combinator. In May 2018 it raised an $18.6 million Series A led by Goodwater Capital, with Y Combinator, FundersClub and others, and said it had more than 250,000 subscribers and was profitable. Beauty Matter put total funding at $28.7 million.

Scentbird has since broadened. In October 2022 it bought Drift, a car air freshener subscription with more than 60,000 subscribers, its first acquisition. Modern Retail reported in December 2025 that Scentbird made more than $100 million in revenue in 2024, citing the Business of Fashion, and that it was building a licensing programme with exclusive fragrances for Marvel, Strawberry Shortcake and a John Wick car freshener with Drift.

On pricing: Scentbird's homepage in late 2025 listed the subscription at $17.95 a month, with a discounted first month of $8.97 as an introductory offer. Prices change, and its site blocked our checks in October 2026, so confirm the current price on scentbird.com.

This page is research, not a review. We have not subscribed; facts come from the sources listed below.
